source_review.notes: Checked all seven official/specification sources. AsyncAPI 3.1.0 supports the application-centered model, send/receive direction, servers, channels, operations, messages, replies, correlation, components, schemas, security, traits, extensions, and bindings. It explicitly warns against mechanically deriving a sender document from a receiver document and distinguishes channel organization from application operations. Official binding and JSON-schema repositories support pinned protocol/tool validation. JSON Schema 2020-12 and CloudEvents 1.0.2 support the referenced payload/envelope profiles, while RFC 3986 supports durable URI application/reference identities.

evidence: Checked document graph A, servers S, channels C, operations O, messages M, components K, references R, resolve/surface functions, runtime B, policy P, declared D, operation sets U_D/U_B, and version tuple V for consistent meaning.
Confirmed graph, set difference, tuple, and semantic conformance notation matches prose.
Confirmed application, server, channel, operation, message, binding, component, and contract drift are separately defined.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Equality symbols are explicitly qualified as semantic agreement under documented environment mappings.

evidence: Confirmed the 3.1.0 spec, 1.0.2 CloudEvents profile, and version-tuple values are identifiers rather than arithmetic claims.
Checked that ten distinct worked examples and five exercise-answer pairs are present.
Confirmed all ordered delivery-pipeline and mechanism steps are complete and sequential.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No throughput, latency, retention, partition, or reliability value is asserted as universal.

evidence: Constructed valid-document/wrong-direction trace proving structural validation cannot establish application perspective or ACL correctness.
Constructed generated-consumer/early-ack crash trace proving type generation cannot establish behavioural delivery safety.
Constructed mutable-reference rebuild trace proving unpinned external schemas break reproducibility without visible contract diff.
Confirmed U_B minus U_D identifies observed undeclared drift while U_D minus U_B needs an observation-window caveat.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Reasoning separates structural, behavioural, deployment, policy, and observed conformance.

evidence: Reviewed producer, consumer, processor, adapter, broker/direct server, regional/environment servers, parameterized channels, message subsets, request/reply, progress/terminal outcomes, and multi-format schemas.

Reviewed wrong direction, missing message, trait conflict, reference cycle/mutation, parser-generator-binding mismatch, schema/registry outage, broker drift, ACL change, early ack, duplicate/reorder/poison/redrive, reply timeout, and rollback.

Reviewed credential/example leakage, arbitrary address/reply routing, cross-tenant channel use, untrusted schema resolution, deserialization/compression, high-cardinality channels/tags, generation supply chain, and public/internal documentation exposure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans document structure, application semantics, deployment, independent tooling, partial failure, and adversarial inputs.

evidence: Confirmed each document has one application perspective/owner/version and operations use send/receive relative to it.
Confirmed channels separate semantic key from deployed address/parameters and operations explicitly select implemented messages.
Confirmed schemas/content/bindings/security/replies/correlation/classification/bounds are pinned and behaviour is not inferred from syntax.
Confirmed declared contract, registry, IaC/ACL policy, generated artifacts, producer/consumer behavior, and observations are reconciled through delivery/runtime gates.
invariant_checking.notes: Infrastructure properties outside binding coverage remain linked and reconciled rather than invented as unsupported fields.

evidence: Reviewed direction counterexample and confirmed a structurally valid receive operation can contradict an emitting runtime and policy.
Reviewed early-ack counterexample and confirmed generated decoding does not prove durable application acceptance.
Reviewed producer/receiver non-inversion argument and confirmed server/channel/security/binding/description differences prevent mechanical derivation.
Reviewed drift set relations and confirmed stale declarations require observation/lifecycle evidence before removal.
proof_review.notes: Proof arguments do not claim AsyncAPI itself enforces delivery, order, replay, idempotency, authorization, or business outcome.

evidence: Confirmed AsyncAPI core, bindings, schema profiles, broker/IaC policy, organization extensions, and runtime behaviour are identified as different layers.
Confirmed application API version, AsyncAPI spec version, schema version, binding version, protocol version, tool version, and deployment build are not conflated.
Confirmed generation, documentation, parsing, schema compatibility, contract tests, reconciliation, and operational evidence have distinct claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Normative format mechanics, implementation recommendations, and deployment-specific obligations remain distinct.

evidence: All seven sources were retrieved or checked on 2026-09-02, with AsyncAPI 3.1.0 and CloudEvents 1.0.2 pinned.
No toolchain, broker, parser, generator, binding, or registry interoperability is asserted without tests.
Actual application documents, generated output, broker/IaC/ACLs, producer-consumer behavior, observation windows, and fault recovery remain explicit deployment evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production AsyncAPI catalog, broker, registry, IaC stack, or runtime telemetry was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed application scope/perspective, metadata, servers, channels, operations, messages, replies/correlation, components/traits/references, bindings, security/privacy, delivery pipeline, runtime drift, and evolution as one coherent contract model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through pinned parser/linter/generator/bindings, immutable schema references, resolved golden artifacts, synthetic examples, schema/consumer matrices, broker integration and negative/fault tests, IaC/ACL reconciliation, catalog publication, canary rollout, telemetry, and restore drills.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module begins with perspective and document graph, develops every core contract surface, then connects it to delivery and runtime evidence. Ten examples cover distinct modeling/drift cases; five exercises progress from one application through CI/CD and multi-application catalog design with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
